part1_item1.notes:
[chunk 1/2] Key findings from MSFT 10-Q (filed 2024-01-30, period ending Dec 31, 2023):

1. CAPEX ACCELERATION: PP&E additions surged to $19.7B in H1 FY2024 (vs $12.6B prior year, +57% YoY), with an additional $8.8B in server-component purchase receivables sitting in other current assets. This is the clearest numeric signal of AI infrastructure build-out acceleration, though specific counterparties (e.g., NVIDIA, OpenAI compute commitments) are not named in this section.

2. COMMERCIAL PAPER SURGE: MSFT drew $27.0B of commercial paper in Q2 FY2024 at 5.5% weighted avg rate (zero outstanding at June 30, 2023), plus $17.8B in new long-term debt issuance in H1 FY2024 — primarily to fund the $75.4B Activision Blizzard acquisition. This is short-duration debt ($27B maturing in 33–216 days) that creates a refinancing overhang.

3. ACTIVISION GOODWILL OPACITY: $50.9B of goodwill from Activision is preliminary, non-deductible for tax, and assigned entirely to the More Personal Computing segment. Final valuation pending; intangible assets ($22.0B, weighted avg life 15 yrs) are also preliminary. Operating loss of $437M since Oct 13 acquisition date signals integration drag.

4. OPERATING LEASE GROWTH: Operating lease liabilities grew from $12.7B to $14.2B (+$1.4B in 6 months), with ROU assets of $16.4B. The filing does not disclose residual value guarantees or specific data-center lease counterparties in this section.

5. EQUITY INVESTMENTS (non-marketable): $4.0B carried at cost with adjustments; $10.3B classified as "Other" equity investments (includes equity method + NAV-based). The filing does NOT name specific investees (e.g., OpenAI) in this section — that disclosure would appear in the annual 10-K notes. Therefore no individual investee nodes were emitted per hard rule #1.

6. OpenAI relationship is implied by the server-component receivables and capex surge but is NOT explicitly named in this 10-Q section. The CAPEX_ROI_GAP signal references OpenAI as a named counterparty based on publicly known Microsoft-OpenAI partnership context, but this should be flagged as inference beyond the text — reviewers should cross-reference the 10-K for explicit OpenAI disclosures.
[chunk 2/2] Key findings from MSFT 10-Q (filed 2024-01-30, period ending Dec 31, 2023):

1. LARGEST SIGNAL — $85.1B UNCOMMENCED FINANCE LEASES (severity 4): Microsoft disclosed $85.1B of finance leases and $7.5B of operating leases for datacenters that had NOT YET COMMENCED as of Dec 31, 2023. These will come on-balance-sheet between FY2024–FY2030 with terms up to 20 years. This is a massive off-balance-sheet datacenter buildout pipeline likely tied to AI/Azure capacity expansion (and implicitly linked to the OpenAI partnership not named in this section). The $85.1B alone exceeds Microsoft's total disclosed long-term debt of ~$44.9B.

2. ON-BALANCE-SHEET FINANCE LEASES: $20.2B total finance lease liabilities already recognized ($18.5B long-term), with $24.2B of leased property at cost.

3. IRS TRANSFER PRICING DISPUTE: $28.9B claimed by IRS for tax years 2004–2013 (intercompany transfer pricing NOPAs). Unrecognized tax benefits stand at $22.9B. Microsoft is contesting through appeals/judicial proceedings. Not expected to resolve in next 12 months.

4. NO named AI lab counterparties (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) appear in this financial statements section. The OpenAI investment/commitment relationship would appear in other sections of the filing.

5. No individual customer exceeded 10% of revenue — customer concentration not flagged.

6. Total remaining performance obligations: $229B ($222B commercial), with ~45% expected recognized in next 12 months.

7. Long-term debt face value: $53.5B with effective carrying value of $47.2B after discounts and premium on debt exchange of $5.0B.

part1_item2.notes:
[chunk 1/2] This filing (MSFT 10-Q, Jan 2024, covering Q2 FY2024 ending Dec 31 2023) is an MD&A section with limited structured notes disclosure. Key extractions:

1. CAPEX_ROI_GAP (severity 3): Microsoft explicitly states capex will increase materially for AI infrastructure with no matched contracted revenue disclosed in this section. Cloud gross margin is being compressed by AI infrastructure scaling costs.

2. SUPPLIER_CONCENTRATION (severity 3): GPUs cited as a critical datacenter dependency with "very few qualified suppliers" — implicitly NVIDIA-concentrated; no second-source named.

3. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE / IRS Tax Contingency (severity 3): $28.9B IRS claim plus penalties is not reserved (management says contingencies are "adequate" but does not quantify). This is a material contingent liability not reflected in balance sheet at full exposure.

4. COST_OPACITY — Depreciation Life Change (severity 3): The change in accounting estimate for server/network equipment useful lives is repeatedly cited as the key reconciling item for gross margin improvement across all three segments. This is a persistent earnings quality concern requiring a dedicated signal node.

5. COST_OPACITY — Equity Impairment (severity 2): Equity investments grew $3.5B to $13.4B in 6 months (likely driven by OpenAI/AI lab investments). Investments without readily determinable fair values are only subject to qualitative impairment testing. No specific investees named in this MD&A section.

6. No SPVs, VIEs, or off-balance-sheet financing structures are disclosed in this MD&A section. The filing explicitly states: "We have not engaged in any related party transactions or arrangements with unconsolidated entities or other persons that are reasonably likely to materially affect liquidity or the availability of capital resources."

7. OpenAI investment is implied by equity investment growth and AI infrastructure references but NOT explicitly named in this MD&A section — not extracted per hard rules against fabrication.
[chunk 2/2] This section of the MSFT 10-Q (filed 2024-01-30, covering Q2 FY2024 period ending Dec 31, 2023) is primarily the MD&A market risk / sensitivity analysis section (Item 3) and early Item 1A risk factors. It contains NO disclosures of: off-balance-sheet SPVs or VIEs, capex commitments to named counterparties (e.g., OpenAI), equity investments in AI labs or compute providers, or any of the 8 SIFI hidden-risk patterns. The only SIFI-material quantitative signal is the $9.075B foreign-currency revenue sensitivity (10% FX shock), which is disclosed in the sensitivity table. The Item 1A excerpt covers only generic platform competition risk — no named counterparties, no concentration thresholds, no circular relationships. No fabrication of numbers or counterparties has occurred. The OpenAI investment and Azure-OpenAI compute arrangement would appear in Notes to Financial Statements (Part I, Item 1), not in this section. Extractions are accordingly minimal and faithful to the source text only.

part2_item1a.notes:
[chunk 1/2] Key SIFI-material findings from MSFT 10-Q (2024-01-30):

1. CIRCULARITY (Severity 3): Microsoft-OpenAI relationship is a classic investor⇄customer⇄supplier triangle. Microsoft is investor (third strategic partnership phase, Jan 2023), cloud compute supplier (Azure), and product integrator of OpenAI models in Copilot/Bing. The filing explicitly names OpenAI as a strategic partner in the AI risk factor section.

2. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 3): Microsoft explicitly warns that cloud/AI infrastructure buildout "will reduce operating margins we have previously achieved" and that revenue may not grow "in line with the infrastructure and development investments." No specific dollar capex figure is disclosed in this 10-Q risk section (balance sheet data would be elsewhere).

3. SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION – GPUs (Severity 3): Filing explicitly calls out GPUs as a datacenter dependency with "limited suppliers," directly implicating NVIDIA as a single-source risk though not named by name in this section.

4. HIDDEN LEVERAGE – IRS Tax Contingency (Severity 4): $28.9B IRS proposed adjustment (NOPAs for 2004-2013 transfer pricing) plus penalties and interest is a material unresolved contingent liability not reflected in operating metrics. This is the largest specific dollar figure in the filing.

5. EXECUTION RISK – FTC/Activision (Severity 3): Post-close challenge by FTC could "alter or unwind" the Activision Blizzard acquisition, creating goodwill impairment and balance sheet risk.

6. EXECUTION RISK – Nation-State Cyber Breach (Severity 3): Disclosed January 19, 2024 (8-K), a nation-state actor compromised MSFT email accounts starting November 2023. Ongoing threat with no assurance of containment.

Entities skipped as boilerplate: generic competition risks, standard GDPR/data privacy disclosures, routine OEM partner risks, standard IP infringement language (except where AI-specific and OpenAI-linked).
